To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a new meta-learning framework, CAML, for few-shot learning that uses conditional transformations based on a metric that is trained to reflect class dependencies; (2) we empirically show that CAML achieves competitive results on miniImageNet, and (3) we provide an analysis that explains why CAML performs well.

(i) CAML is a meta-learning approach that uses a conditional transformation of the feature representations based on the inter-class dependencies, which is trained on the label space, and (ii) this conditional transformation enables a more disentangled representation space and achieves competitive results.
we present a novel meta-learning framework that can be used to improve representation learning in the few-shot learning context by explicitly incorporating label structure.
